mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.25% signals an accommodative monetary policy that compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.25% (5-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering negative equity returns as corporate earnings growth expectations decline over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp monthly.

mechanism_narrative: Joint monthly growth in housing starts (HOUST) and real sales (RSAFS) exceeding 0.1% each signals robust consumer demand expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days through strengthened corporate revenue outlook.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both rise > 0.1% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS rise > 0.1% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, a monthly industrial production decline exceeding 0.5% signals manufacturing slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns as profit margins contract under demand uncertainty.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO declines > 0.5% in late-cycle expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 0.1% indicates expanding residential construction demand, correlating with stronger consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when HOUST rises > 0.1% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly Consumer Price Index increase exceeding 0.5% signals accelerating inflation, prompting monetary tightening that reduces equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous monthly payroll growth exceeding 0.5% (PAYEMS) and unemployment decline exceeding 0.1 percentage points (UNRATE) signals labor market tightening, driving positive S&P 500 returns through wage growth and consumption expansion.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 0.5% and UNRATE falls > 0.1pp in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS rises > 0.5% and UNRATE falls > 0.1pp monthly.

mechanism_narrative: In supply shock regime, a monthly industrial production decline exceeding 1.0% signals manufacturing contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns as supply chain disruptions reduce corporate profitability over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO declines > 1.0% in supply shock regime.
